hook: SCP-087 is a staircase, and the main file tells you little more than that. The real experience is in the linked exploration logs, so read them in order, ideally somewhere quiet. Each descent begins the same way, which is exactly why the small differences land.
whyItMatters:
087 is one of the wiki's clearest examples of horror built from space and sound rather than a visible monster: a repeating geometry, a light that won't reach far enough, and a voice that never gets any closer. It shows how much dread a document can generate through structure and withholding alone.

It is also a good example of the wiki's multi-page format. The main file is short and points to separate exploration transcripts, so the full experience depends on clicking through to them.
thingsToNotice:
The specification is the trap: every flight is thirteen steps at a 38-degree pitch, every landing turns you around completely, and you can only ever see about a flight and a half ahead, so the geometry itself keeps whatever is below out of sight. Even the light is capped, since anything stronger than 75 watts seems to get swallowed by the stairwell.

Two things wait down there, and the file keeps them apart. A child's crying seems to come from roughly 200 meters down, yet no descent brings anyone closer, and Exploration IV went deeper than the building or the ground under it could possibly hold. SCP-087-1, a featureless face without pupils, nostrils or a mouth, appeared to every D-class explorer, and the file insists it is not the one doing the pleading.

The ending lives in the gaps: the fourth exploration log is expunged, all entry has been banned since, and for two weeks afterward people on campus heard knocking from behind the disguised closet door at a steady one-to-two-second beat. The Foundation answered with six centimeters of foam padding, after which the reports stopped, which is not quite the same thing as the knocking stopping.
